claims.claim: Suppress manifest workflow-confirmation notes when establishing the initial manifest snapshot, while still running applicable manifest and architecture validation.
claims.trigger: Post-tool shell handling with no valid saved manifest snapshot in an available Git state directory
claims.exceptions: Later snapshots can produce notes; validator errors and warnings remain reportable on the initial run.
claims.enforcement_effect: The !delta.initial guard omits changeNotes; it does not exempt manifest validation.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Prior claims require unexplained-change reminders and mention initial full validation, but do not register initial reminder suppression.
No-Git comparison absence, revision-change exemption and project-change workflow routing differ from the initial-snapshot condition inside a Git worktree.

claims.comparison_reason: All three union claims were considered; initial full validation does not entail absence of workflow notes. Quote overlap in RULE-M1-0085 is insufficient equivalence.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: An unrecognized shell command changes a valid package manifest before the first snapshot exists. Validation can pass and no workflow-confirmation note is generated; the same change after a saved snapshot can generate one.

claims.claim: For direct edits of non-package.json dependency manifests, emit the dependency workflow reminder only when replacement/content text contains the recognized dependency tokens.
claims.trigger: Write/Edit/MultiEdit of a manifest through fileChecks(rel, changedText(toolInput))
claims.exceptions: package.json always satisfies the reminder predicate; separate manifest/architecture findings may still block.
claims.enforcement_effect: changedText at lines 39-44 takes content/new_string/edits[].new_string, not old_string; deleting a PackageReference without a matching replacement token need not emit this reminder.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Prior dependency-edit reminder and manifest-check claims omit the new-text-only detection scope.
Removal command markers concern shell operations, not deletion by direct editing of XML manifest text.

claims.comparison_reason: The prior actions imply a broader dependency-edit reminder than the actual token predicate. No equivalent direct-edit deletion exception found across three baselines.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: Edit a .csproj by replacing a complete PackageReference line with an empty string, leaving a valid project. The dependency entry was removed, but changedText is empty and this reminder is absent.

claims.claim: Report internal PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure/Stop hook failures via stderr and exit 1 without emitting a blocking decision.
claims.trigger: Caught internal exception in post-tool-use.js lines224-225 or stop.js lines108-109
claims.exceptions: PreToolUse uses denyOnFailure and is fail-closed; tool-command failure with successful hook execution uses separate diagnostic handling.
claims.enforcement_effect: Source defines this as visible non-blocking failure policy (lines5-7); runtime host behavior is not experimentally tested.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Explicitly calls visible non-blocking Post/Stop failure reporting implementation behavior.
Fail-closed Pre guard and repair instruction differ; BF0041 addresses ordinary tool failures receiving context, not internal hook failure abandoning checks.

claims.comparison_reason: An operational enforcement exception was dismissed rather than registered. Independently observable output/exit behavior changes what happens when checks fail internally.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: An internal exception interrupts Stop before reminders are computed; catch invokes fail and exits1 instead of a decision:block asking the assistant to address co-change findings.

claims.claim: Rename/copy status handling discards the second pathname, potentially excluding the old model location from Stop co-change applicability.
claims.trigger: Git porcelain-v1 -z entry marked R/C consumed by changedFiles and then Stop reminders
claims.exceptions: Other changed paths or destination matching model patterns may still trigger reminders.
claims.enforcement_effect: Observed i++ skips a status pathname; whether a real model move evades its old-path reminder depends on status ordering and selected module patterns.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Git-state co-change detection and filename reminders do not explicitly register old-path omission for rename/copy.

claims.comparison_reason: No equivalent atomic old-path exclusion found, but source branch alone does not establish the full runtime consequence.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A model file is renamed out of a selected module model glob without migration/seed edits. If only destination is returned, the original model-path trigger can disappear.
claims.open_question: Can frozen evidence establish porcelain pathname ordering and actual selected-glob applicability for this scenario without assuming external runtime behavior?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Executable actual-trigger pass: inspect module patterns and use a pure copied-parser fixture; retain distinction between fixture behavior and live Git behavior.

claims.claim: Successful post-tool diagnostics can return a block decision, while PostToolUseFailure reports the same messages as additional context.
claims.trigger: Messages exist after registered post-tool execution
claims.exceptions: Internal hook errors use separate fail handling.
claims.enforcement_effect: Includes WARN as well as ERROR through report filtering.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Both explicitly represent success blocking including warnings and failed-tool context exception.

claims.comparison_reason: Same event distinction and severity already registered; no new finding.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A warning after success blocks, whereas it adds context after command failure.
